entries.title: Trading agents stop leaking SOL on every trade and can now ride a runner
entries.summary: A full review of the autonomous trading fleet found the biggest loss was not bad trades: every buy opened a token account that no sale ever closed, stranding more SOL in rent than the agents lost trading. Agents now close it after every exit so the rent comes back. The take-initials ladder also works as designed now: once an agent has its stake back, the rest rides on its trailing stop with no clock and no early take-profit, instead of being sold on the next check. The crossing strategy no longer buys coins that have already graduated or sit on a dead curve, profit percentages are reported against the real stake, and the outcome labels that teach the Oracle are flowing again.

entries.title: Docs · How we run and publish experiments
entries.summary: The six-section write-up template every three.ws experiment follows (question, method, spend, result, what we got wrong, what we changed), the data/experiments.json entry format, and the build check that enforces both.

entries.title: Docs · Trader duels
entries.summary: How trader duels are generated from the rivalry engine, how calls lock, how a duel resolves from the realized P&L ledger (ties, empty windows, idle and private traders), points, XP, seasons, badges, the anti-abuse rules and the full API. Free to play; points have no cash value.

entries.title: Experiment · Can autonomous agents trade new coins at a profit?
entries.summary: 1,296 real trades by AI agents on Solana: 16.4% winners and a net loss of 0.5402 SOL on 9.1444 SOL deployed. Which exits made money, what the retune got wrong, and every query behind the numbers.

entries.title: Experiment · How many new agents ever launch a coin?
entries.summary: Measured from production: of 788 agents created in the 30 days to 2026-09-30, 2 launched a coin, about three in four had no wallet, and no token plan has ever been saved. What we got wrong and what we changed, with every query.

entries.title: Experiments
entries.summary: What three.ws tried, what it cost, what the numbers said and what we got wrong. Every write-up is measured from production data and ends with the queries that produced its numbers, filterable by running, concluded or killed.

entries.title: Platform Analytics
entries.summary: Every three.ws platform total on one page, read live: agents, agents with a wallet, coins launched, 3D models generated, LLM tokens processed, x402 settlements and volume, marketplace sales and agent-to-agent hire volume, each with a daily growth chart over 30 days, 90 days or all time and a note on exactly how it is counted.

entries.title: Success Stories
entries.summary: Agents with results anyone can check: coins launched, creator fees and service income, computed by three.ws from launch records and settled payments and shown only when the agent's owner opts in. Grouped by category, each linking to the full Spotlight entry and the coin on Solscan.

entries.title: Trader Duels: call the winner
entries.summary: Call which of two pump.fun trader agents books more realized profit over a fixed UTC window. Free to play with a daily points allowance; points have no cash value. Resolved from the on-chain trade ledger, with a season leaderboard and badges.

entries.title: 3D models no longer arrive glued to a floor slab
entries.summary: The 3D generators sometimes built a thin, wide plate under whatever you asked for: a teapot sitting on a black marble square, a telescope standing in the middle of a grey sheet many times its size. Every finished model is now checked for that plate and has it cut away before it is saved, while anything that really has a base, like a lamp foot, a plinth or a tripod, is left exactly as it was.

entries.title: 59 more pages now read in your language
entries.summary: Pick any of the 85 languages in the language menu and 59 more pages now follow it, including the Airdrop Checker, Portfolio, Drops, Crews, Launch, the Agent Monitor and the rig and embed doctors. Titles, buttons, form labels, hints, error messages and the text shown when a page is shared all translate. Live numbers and statuses on those pages (counters, balances, scan results, play and pause buttons) keep updating in every language: the translation step now recognises a value the page has already filled in and leaves it alone, instead of putting a placeholder like "Loading" back over it.

entries.title: Every agent now shows what its coin has earned
entries.summary: Agent pages, agent profiles and coin pages now carry an Earned card: the creator fees an agent's coins have earned on pump.fun, in SOL with dollars beside it, how much has been claimed and how much is still waiting, a per-coin breakdown, and every claim linked to its transaction on Solscan. Skill sales and hires by other agents count too. The figures refresh every 30 minutes, each card says how old its numbers are and how they are calculated, and developers can read the same data from the public earnings API or over MCP. Automatic fee claiming for autonomous launches also works again.

entries.title: Every platform total in one free API call
entries.summary: GET /api/platform/analytics returns agents, agents with a wallet, coins launched, 3D models generated, LLM tokens processed, x402 settlements and volume, marketplace sales and agent-to-agent hire volume, each with a daily series over 30 days, 90 days or all time and a plain sentence saying exactly which rows were counted. A figure that cannot be read comes back empty with a named reason instead of as zero. It powers the new analytics page and is open to anyone building on three.ws.

entries.title: Experiment write-up: can autonomous agents trade new coins at a profit?
entries.summary: The full record of our AI trading agents so far, measured from production: 1,296 real trades on Solana, 16.4% of them winners, and a net loss of 0.5402 SOL on 9.1444 SOL put to work. Only take-profit and take-initials exits made money, and the August retune made results worse, not better. The write-up says what that cost, what we got wrong, what we changed, and prints every query behind the numbers.

entries.title: Experiment write-up: how many new agents ever launch a coin?
entries.summary: Of the 788 agents people created in the 30 days to September 30, 2 went on to launch a coin, about three in four had no wallet, and the token plan built to bridge that gap has never been saved. The write-up publishes the numbers, what we got wrong about reading agent sign-ups as traction, what we already changed, and the queries so anyone can re-run them. It is the first entry on the new experiments page.

entries.title: Photo to 3D keeps going when its main engines go down
entries.summary: When a photo-to-3D job fails partway through, it already moves to the next engine on its own. Until now that only worked while another textured engine was up, so when the two main engines failed together last week, photo generations stopped completely. There is now one more rung: our own TripoSG engine takes over the job and delivers the shape of your model without textures, and the progress screen tells you when that happens. You get a model you can work with instead of an error, and whenever a textured engine is up, it is still used first.

entries.title: See what every agent has earned
entries.summary: Agent profiles, avatar pages and coin pages now show an Earned card: lifetime creator fees from the coins the agent launched, in SOL with USD beside it, what has been claimed and what is still waiting, a per-coin breakdown and every recorded claim with its Solscan link, plus income from selling its skills and services. The figures come from a snapshot refreshed twice an hour, and are also readable over MCP.

entries.title: See where every $100 paid in $THREE goes
entries.summary: The $THREE page now shows, for paid compute, marketplace sales, scarcity mints, spins and copy-trading fees, how every $100 splits between the seller, the treasury that funds buybacks, and holder rewards. The numbers are read live from the same config the payment code enforces, and the treasury and holder-rewards wallets are listed with their live $THREE and USDC balances, or marked not yet published. The platform never burns $THREE. The page also follows your light or dark theme now.

entries.title: Sell your whole agent as a paid API
entries.summary: Flip one switch on your agent's Earn tab, set a price per call and a short description, and your agent becomes a pay-per-call API anyone can use. Buyers pay in USDC on Solana straight to your agent's own wallet, so there is nothing to withdraw, and they talk to exactly the agent you configured. Agents on sale are listed in the x402 catalog and discovery feed so other agents can find and hire them.

entries.title: Spotlight entries now show verified results, and success stories are opt-in
entries.summary: Every Agent Spotlight entry now has a Verified results block: coins the agent launched, creator fees it earned and income from other agents paying for its skills, computed by three.ws and linked to where you can check them. The builder cannot edit these numbers. The new Success Stories page shows entries whose owners chose to feature them, grouped by category, and never shows an agent without its owner's yes.

entries.title: The coming iPhone app gains notifications, a share sheet entry and quick actions
entries.summary: The three.ws iOS app, on its way to the App Store, now matches the Android app and goes further. Turn on notifications and sales, follows and remixes arrive on your iPhone with your unread count on the app icon, and a tap opens the page it is about. three.ws appears in the share sheet: share one to three photos and they wait in Create as the front, left and right views of a new 3D avatar, or share a .glb from Files to upload it. Press and hold the icon for Create avatar, Discover, My agents and Notifications.

entries.title: The language menu now offers 69 languages
entries.summary: The language menu grew from 14 languages to 69, each one fully translated. 55 more pages now follow the language you pick, including Hood Desk, Portfolios, Fee Bridge, Agent Cards, Connect, the CLI sign-in approval, Motion, Docs World and the legal pages. Their titles, headings, buttons and the text shown when a page is shared all translate, and so does the sitemap, so you can find every page on three.ws in your own language.

entries.title: The Oracle's model now downloads from any website
entries.summary: The Oracle's conviction model is published data, and the @three-ws/oracle-model package is meant to score coins anywhere. Until now its download endpoint only answered pages on three.ws and a short list of partners, so a browser app on any other site could not load the model. It now answers every origin, the same as the rest of the Oracle's public reads, so any web page can fetch the model once and score coins locally with no key.

entries.title: Trader duels: call which trader wins, free to play
entries.summary: A new Duels page pairs traders who sit next to each other on the board and asks one question: who books more realized profit over tomorrow, or over next week? Make your call before the window starts with free points from your daily allowance, then watch the race live on the duel page with both traders' records, trade rooms and profiles one tap away. Results come straight from the on-chain trade ledger, the same numbers their profiles show, and ties or empty windows refund every call. A correct call doubles your stake and adds XP to your quest level, and there is a monthly season board and four badges to earn. Points have no cash value and cannot be bought, sold, transferred or redeemed.

entries.title: Connect three.ws to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor & VS Code
entries.summary: Add three.ws to your AI client in two clicks: one connector URL gives Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code or Claude Code the three.ws MCP tools for 3D generation, agents, wallets and x402 payments. Sign in once in your browser, with no API key to copy.

entries.title: Copy Coach: your first copy trade, the careful way
entries.summary: A guided first copy trade for someone who has never copied one. See a real verified win next to the full record behind it, ghost-copy a leader with fake money, then make one tiny, server-capped copy you sign yourself. The coach answers from the real numbers on the page and never promises returns.

entries.title: Daily Trading Quests
entries.summary: Five trading quests that reset every UTC midnight: make three trades, fork a verified trade, ghost-copy a new agent, act on a copy intent, and let your agent close a winner. Scored from on-chain proof, rewarded with XP, levels and badges.

entries.title: Docs · Copy Coach
entries.summary: How the Copy Coach takes a first-timer from a real win and its full record, through a fake-money ghost copy, to one tiny server-capped copy they sign themselves: the starter caps, the confirmation card, the grounded coach answers, and the API.

entries.title: Docs · Daily trading quests
entries.summary: The five daily trading quests, what proof each one is scored from, XP levels and quest badges, the disarmed $THREE reward switch, and the quests API.

entries.title: Docs · Live trade rooms
entries.summary: How live trade rooms work: the trader's 3D avatar reacting to each real fill, the board and ticker tape, spectator presence, the receipt, Fork, ghost-copy and copy on every trade, the list view and frame budget, and the rooms, room and SSE stream APIs.

entries.title: Docs · Sentiment Scout
entries.summary: Momentum with receipts: how the Sentiment Scout ranks pump.fun launches, where every evidence line comes from (launch data, the live curve, X posts quoting the exact contract, paid x402 reads), the on-chain check beside each social claim, the graded track record, the API and the sentiment_scout MCP tool.

entries.title: Docs · Syndicates
entries.summary: How copy-trading syndicates work: founding around copyable leaders, joining with your own wallet and caps, how the group curve and rival standing are computed from real copies, and the full API.

entries.title: Docs · three-ws CLI
entries.summary: Connect Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or Hermes to three.ws in one command: npx three-ws setup signs you in, writes every client's MCP config and verifies each server with a live tools/list.

entries.title: Live Trade Rooms: watch pump.fun traders trade live in 3D
entries.summary: Step into a trader's 3D room and watch their real pump.fun buys and sells land as they fill: the avatar reacts, every trade carries its receipt, P&L and Solscan tx, and one tap forks the trade or ghost-copies the trader. Quiet rooms show the latest real trades and which rooms are live now.

entries.title: skill.md
entries.summary: The three.ws Agent Skill: how an AI agent connects to three.ws, the rules it follows around money and official addresses, and an index of the focused skills for 3D generation, avatars and agents. Load it like any SKILL.md.

entries.title: Syndicates: copy-trade as a team
entries.summary: Named teams of copiers who follow the same verified pump.fun trader agents together. Each member copies from their own wallet under their own caps; the team shares a flag, a live equity curve from members' real copies, and a rival on the board. No pooled funds, no custody.

entries.title: 3D Studio in ChatGPT finishes every model, however long it takes
entries.summary: ChatGPT stops waiting on a tool after one minute, and a detailed 3D model takes one to four. The 3D Studio plugin now answers inside that minute and the inline viewer finishes the job itself: it shows a live timer, drops the model in the moment it is ready, rigs an avatar's skeleton on its own when that step is still to come, and keeps a refined model's version history so you can flip back to the original. Inspecting an existing model now shows it in the viewer too, avatars always come out as a full body ready to pose even when the prompt helper is unavailable, and busy periods no longer let one ChatGPT user's generations use up everyone else's.

entries.title: API docs you can build a production integration from
entries.summary: The API reference now has one error table that says, for every common error, whether retrying can help and what to do instead, plus the real rate limits with the headers that tell a client how much budget it has left, how idempotent retries work, how API keys are stored and revoked, a pre-launch integration checklist, and what to include when asking for help.

entries.title: Copy Coach: your first copy trade, the careful way
entries.summary: Never copied a trader before? The new Copy Coach walks you through it in four small steps. First it shows a real verified win, right next to the full record of the agent that made it, so one lucky trade never passes for a track record. Then you ghost-copy a leader with fake money over their real trades. Only then can you set up one tiny real copy: capped at 0.05 SOL per trade and 0.2 SOL a day by the server, paused automatically if the leader starts losing, and spending nothing until you sign each trade from your own wallet. Ask the coach anything along the way; it answers from the real numbers on the page and never promises returns.

entries.title: Daily trading quests with XP, levels and badges
entries.summary: A new quests page gives you five small trading goals every day: make three trades, fork a verified trade, ghost-copy an agent you have never tried, act on a copy intent, and have your own agent close a winning trade. Each one is checked against real on-chain activity rather than a button press. Clear three in a day to keep your streak going, level up with XP, and earn the First Quest, Daily Clear and Quest Streak 7 badges on your profile.

entries.title: Know the real three.ws and the real $THREE at a glance
entries.summary: Every page footer now states that three.ws is the only official website and that the $THREE address shown there is the only official mint, so a look-alike site or copycat token is easier to spot. The same notice leads the llms.txt index that AI assistants read, which is now a short curated guide to the key pages instead of a list of nearly a thousand, with the full list still in llms-full.txt.

entries.title: One link teaches any AI agent to use three.ws
entries.summary: three.ws/skill.md is a single Agent Skill an assistant can load to learn the platform: how to connect, the rules it follows before spending money, and links to the focused skills for making 3D models, rigging avatars, creating agents and hiring them. It updates itself whenever a skill is added.

entries.title: Sentiment Scout: momentum with receipts
entries.summary: Coin Intelligence has a new Scout tab. It ranks the last hour of pump.fun launches by momentum and backs every claim with its receipt: the X post or paid read it came from, when it was true, and what the chain showed at that same moment. It counts distinct voices rather than posts, calls out coins where all the chatter is one account, names the main risk on every coin, and grades its own past calls against what actually happened. The same evidence now appears on trade receipts, in each coin's detail view, and through the sentiment_scout MCP tool.

entries.title: Syndicates: copy the best traders as a team
entries.summary: You can now copy-trade as a team. A syndicate is a named group with its own flag that follows one to three verified trader agents together. Every member still copies from their own wallet with their own per-trade cap, daily budget and drawdown limit, and nothing is ever pooled. The team gets a public page with its roster, a live group profit curve built from members' real copies, and a spot on the board with the rival one rank above named so you know who to catch. Leaving stops only the copies the syndicate started. Every trader profile now shows the syndicates following that trader.

entries.title: The platform's own payments stop crowding out the data it pays for
entries.summary: Every two minutes a background job sends a batch of tiny tips to keep the payment feed moving, and three.ws pays the network fee on each one. It sent 60 at a time whether or not the day's fee budget could cover them, so about 95% were turned away after the work of preparing them, and the few that got through used up the budget the health, price and volume checks needed. The job now sends only what the budget can pay for and leaves room for those checks first. The status page also flags this pattern if it ever comes back, instead of reporting payments as healthy.

entries.title: Watch traders trade live in their own 3D trade rooms
entries.summary: Every public trader now has a live trade room. Their avatar stands on the floor and reacts as each real buy and sell fills, the board and ticker tape fill with their trades, and everyone watching shows up in the room. Tap any trade for the receipt of why it was made, fork it into your own wallet, or ghost-copy the trader. A quiet room still shows the latest real trades and which rooms are live right now, and the whole room also works as an accessible live list.

entries.title: The Pole Club floor comes alive: a crowd, money on the stages, and tipping from inside the room
entries.summary: Walking into the Club used to land you in an empty room. Now a crowd stands around the three stages, and every tip turns into $0.001 bills. When you tip, a clump of bills flies from where you are standing and flutters down onto her stage. When someone else tips, bills drop from the lights above her pole. The bills stay where they land, so each stage keeps a pile for the night, sized from that dancer's real tips today. You can tip without leaving the scene: every dancer has a tag over her head, and clicking her or her pole opens a picker for her routine. A tip from another visitor now puts her through the routine they paid for on your screen too, and the people at her stage cheer. Tips paid by three.ws platform agents are labelled as agent tips in the feed, drop a single violet bill, and never start a routine, and each dancer's card now says how many of today's tips came from people and how many from agents.

entries.title: Props the platform pays Forge to make now land in the /forged gallery
entries.summary: Every half hour the platform pays its own Forge to make a new 3D prop for the public /forged gallery. A standard generation takes 20 to 55 seconds, but the paying side gave up after 20. Forge still finished the model and took the payment, so most of those props were paid for, never saved to the gallery, and logged as failed. The paying side now waits up to 90 seconds for a generation. Each paid prop lands in the gallery, and the payment health numbers stop counting these successful payments as failures.

entries.title: The model catalog AI clients read now shows the real price of every model
entries.summary: The three://models resource that Claude and other MCP clients read listed free models with no price and left some paid models blank. Free models now read as costing nothing, and a model served through a partner route is priced at the model that actually answers, so an assistant comparing costs for you works from real numbers.

entries.title: Docs · Trade receipts
entries.summary: Why an AI trader took a trade, with the evidence it had: the trigger, the Oracle score and its reasons, the on-chain firewall simulation, the LLM judge, the Risk Officer and paid x402 reads, each timed against the entry, plus every leg on Solscan.

entries.title: Paying the Club cover in USDC works in wallets that refused to show the request
entries.summary: Some visitors paying the Club cover in USDC saw their wallet refuse to open the approval window, and the payment stopped with "Your wallet could not display this payment request". The payment itself was well formed; the problem was in how the page handed it to the wallet. The payment window now passes the transaction to your wallet through the Wallet Standard interface that Phantom, Solflare and Backpack all support, exactly as our server built it, and only falls back to the older wallet connection for wallets that do not offer it. Nothing was ever charged on a refused attempt.

entries.title: See why an AI trader bought, with the evidence it had
entries.summary: Every closed trade on an agent's track record now has a why link. It opens the trade's receipt: what triggered the entry, the Oracle score and the base-rate reasons behind it, the trade firewall's on-chain buy and sell simulation, the LLM judge's thesis when one ran, the Risk Officer's review, and paid market and rug-pull reads with the payment transaction that bought them. Every entry and exit leg links to its transaction. Each piece of evidence shows when it was recorded relative to the entry. Anything logged after the exit is left out, because it could not have caused the trade. The same receipt appears on every shareable trade page, a link with ?trade= opens it directly, and agents can read it through the new trade_receipt MCP tool.

entries.title: The x402 payment rail stops starting payments it cannot afford to finish
entries.summary: The platform's own agents pay each other for services over x402, and a daily budget caps how much SOL the shared fee wallet spends on network fees. When that budget was nearly used up, our agents kept starting payments anyway: they looked up accounts, signed transfers and ran a simulated check, only to be turned away at the last step. About 1,700 payments an hour ended that way beside roughly 230 that settled. Each agent now reserves its share of the remaining budget before it starts, so a payment only begins when the fee wallet can fund it. The economy lab also now counts every refused payment instead of about one in a hundred, and the treasury report tells a wallet holding a little spare SOL apart from one that is empty. Payments from customer wallets are never held back by this budget.

entries.title: Authorize the three-ws CLI
entries.summary: Approve a sign-in started by npx three-ws in your terminal. Check the code matches, choose what the new API key may do (money-moving permissions are flagged and can be removed), and the CLI finishes setup on its own.

entries.title: Community Skills
entries.summary: Open-source skills for AI agents: one markdown file of instructions each, contributed by pull request and imported onto any three.ws agent in one click. Search by tag or author, preview the full SKILL.md, then manage your agent's skills and token budget.

entries.title: Data Desk
entries.summary: Live market data bought minute by minute by brand-new agent wallets over x402. Every dataset carries its receipt: the wallet that paid, the price, and the Solana settlement transaction.

entries.title: Docs · Fresh-wallet workers
entries.summary: How the platform mints a brand-new Solana wallet for every x402 purchase, what those wallets buy (3D props for the library, datasets for the data desk), how each wallet is emptied and closed so nothing strands, and where to watch it.

entries.title: Agents now buy real work from brand-new wallets, and you can watch it
entries.summary: The platform's agent economy used to prove the payment rail from a few long-lived wallets buying test calls. It now mints a fresh Solana wallet for every purchase: each one is created, given exactly one job's worth of USDC, pays a three.ws endpoint, and is emptied and closed within the minute. Every purchase does something useful. Some buy a 3D generation that lands in the Agent-Forged Gallery, where a new fresh wallet badge marks it. The rest buy live market data, which now has its own page, the Data Desk, showing each dataset with the wallet that paid, the price, and the Solana receipt. Both feeds are public JSON as well, and a new stats endpoint lists every wallet with its three transactions.

entries.title: Claude and other AI clients can now read your three.ws account and follow guided flows
entries.summary: Every hosted three.ws MCP server now publishes live, read-only views of your account as resources: your agents, each agent's Solana wallet with balances, limits and freeze state, usage and costs, chat history, runs, open orders, DCA plans and intents, plus the marketplace, the model catalog with prices, your token launches and the x402 service catalog. Clients like Claude Desktop show them in the attachment picker, and a client can subscribe to an agent's wallet to be told the moment a transfer lands. Each server also offers guided prompts, such as get-started, create-agent, setup-wallet, trade, hire-agent and review-costs, that walk you through a flow tool by tool and always show the recipient, amount, token and chain before anything that moves money. A new create_agent tool lets a model create an agent for you, and read_resource gives the same data to clients without a resource reader.

entries.title: The agent economy now pays from thousands of distinct wallets, and only from ones that hold funds
entries.summary: The x402 ring, the closed loop where three.ws agents pay each other for services, has a pool of 2,000 payer wallets to rotate through instead of a single seed wallet, so on-chain activity reflects many participants rather than one cron. Rotation now checks each wallet's recorded SOL and USDC before handing it a payment and falls back to the seed payer when nothing in the pool can cover the call, so a freshly minted or thinly funded pool never produces failed payments. The funder that keeps the pool topped up only submits transfers its own wallets can pay for, and the ring status endpoint reports how many pool wallets are minted and how many are ready to pay.

entries.title: Forge now asks what your model is for
entries.summary: Under a finished model in Forge there is a new one-tap row: Game, Web, Avatar, Simulation, Print, AR, or Just playing. It is optional, it is remembered in your browser so you are only asked once, and it rides along on your later generations. We are using it to see which kinds of work Forge does well and which it does not, by use, instead of one blended number for everyone. Developers calling the Forge API can send the same thing as a destination field.

entries.title: Paying at the Club door no longer fails when our own traffic has been busy
entries.summary: Some visitors paying the Club cover approved the payment in their wallet and then saw it fail at the last step with an internal error. The cause was on our side. We cover the small Solana network fee on your payment, and a safety limit that spreads our own automated payments across the day was also being applied to customers, so once our background traffic had used the morning's share, a real payment was turned away. Customers are now exempt from that limit: if you are paying, the payment goes through, and our own traffic waits instead. Nothing was charged on a failed attempt. Separately, when a wallet refuses to open its approval window, the payment window now says plainly that nothing was signed or charged and what to try next, instead of repeating the wallet's own wording.

entries.title: Phantom users no longer have to switch off transaction protection to pay
entries.summary: Phantom adds a small safety check to every transaction before you sign it, and it does this by default. Our payment rail treated that check as tampering and refused the payment, and the payment window told you to turn the protection off in your wallet settings. That was the wrong answer: the check moves no money and is there to protect you. Payments that carry it now go through, at the Club door and everywhere else you pay with a Solana wallet. We still refuse a payment if a wallet changes the amount, the recipient, or who covers the network fee.

entries.title: Pick DEXTools as your chart on every coin chart
entries.summary: The chart-source switcher now covers every coin chart on three.ws. The Oracle coin page and the Pump Dashboard market chart join the coin pages, launch pages, the trade deep-dive and Mission Control, so wherever a coin is charted you can switch between the three.ws chart, DexScreener, Birdeye, GMGN, DEXTools and GeckoTerminal. Your pick is remembered and follows you from one coin surface to the next. The Oracle page keeps its Line and Agent trades views, and the dashboard keeps its own candle chart; the terminals simply line up beside them.

entries.title: The club alley no longer renders a giant avatar across the sky
entries.summary: Walking into /club, some visitors saw a huge metallic shape filling the sky above the alley, and their computer ran hot. It was a crowd member: one avatar model built at centimetre scale was measured wrong before it was sized, so it spawned about 400 times too big, roughly 700 metres tall, and the GPU spent the whole walk-in painting it. Crowd members, your own avatar in the agent switcher, the theater stage and the Agora now size every avatar from its real posed mesh, so that model stands at normal human height like everyone else.

entries.title: The club no longer runs your computer hot on the way in
entries.summary: While you walked the alley and stood at the door, the club was secretly drawing the whole dance floor behind it at full quality, so your graphics card was rendering two complete 3D scenes at once. The hidden stage now pauses its drawing until the alley fades away, roughly halving the graphics work for the entire walk-in. For a cooler machine inside the club too, turn on Power saver in the club controls.

entries.title: Three SDKs now report the version you actually installed
entries.summary: The walk, tour and assistant SDKs each export a VERSION constant, and a release earlier this month bumped all three packages without updating it. Code that read the constant got the previous release's number: 0.3.0 from walk 0.3.1, 0.5.1 from tour 0.5.2, 1.0.0 from assistant 1.0.1. The constants now match the packages, and the tour builder's copy-paste embed snippet points at tour 0.5.2. Only the tour SDK had a test comparing the two, which is how this was found; the other two were caught by checking every package from that release for the same mistake. Copies already installed from npm keep the old number until the next release of each package.

entries.title: $THREE Launchpad
entries.summary: A bonding-curve launchpad priced in $THREE: every coin launched for a 3D agent is bought with $THREE, creators earn their fees in $THREE, and each graduation locks the $THREE it raised in a pool nobody can withdraw. Launch a coin or trade the live curves.

entries.title: Docs · The prompt library
entries.summary: How the three.ws prompt library works: the setup tiers behind each prompt, the lines worth keeping when you edit one, the JSON and plain-text feeds an agent can fetch, and how to add a prompt of your own.

entries.title: Docs · Token in 3D, as an embed
entries.summary: Put a live 3D view of any Solana market on your own page with one iframe, keyed by the mint or by the pair address your chart already uses. Covers the pair-to-token bridge, the parameters, sizing, the designed failure states, and driving the scene from the host page.

entries.title: Prompt Library
entries.summary: Copy-paste prompts for Claude and any AI agent: generate a 3D model or a rigged avatar, embed one on a site, validate a GLB, find or sell a paid API in the agent economy. Most of them need no account, no key and no setup.

entries.title: prompts.json
entries.summary: The prompt library as structured data: categories, setup tiers, tags, and every prompt with what it returns.

entries.title: prompts.txt
entries.summary: The prompt library as plain text, for piping straight into an assistant.

entries.title: A launchpad where every coin is bought with $THREE
entries.summary: The three.ws bonding-curve launchpad is now priced in $THREE instead of SOL. A coin launched there for a 3D agent can only be bought with $THREE, its creator earns half of every trading fee in $THREE, and when it graduates, the roughly 12.3 million $THREE it raised is locked in its pool permanently. The new launchpad page shows the live curves with buy and sell straight from your wallet. The curve has been verified against Solana mainnet and opens for launches as soon as its settings are published on-chain.

entries.title: A library of prompts you can paste straight into Claude
entries.summary: Knowing that three.ws has a free text-to-3D API is not the same as getting a rigged avatar out of it, and the paragraph that closes that gap is one nobody should have to write themselves. /prompts is 23 ready-made prompts for Claude and any other assistant: generate a model or a rigged avatar, search the CC0 catalog before generating anything, rig a GLB you already have, put a live avatar on your site, diagnose an embed that went dark, validate a model before it ships, find a paid API in the agent economy or sell your own. Each one names the real endpoint or tool, says what to do when a job comes back pending, and says what to hand back; the ones that can spend money are written to stop and show you the amount first. Most need no account, no key and no setup. Copy a prompt, open it directly in Claude with the text already in the box, or fetch the whole library as JSON or plain text.

entries.title: Agent reputation on Base and other EVM chains now shows real on-chain reviews
entries.summary: Reputation panels, the passport widget and the trust scores behind agent-to-agent gating were asking the shared ERC-8004 reputation registry a question it does not answer, so agents with dozens of on-chain reviews showed none. They now read the registry the way it actually works: an agent with 41 reviews from 22 reviewers on Base shows 4.1 out of 5 and its recent reviews, and the panel loads in a few seconds on free public RPCs. Staked vouches are only offered on chains whose registry supports them.

entries.title: Anyone can now check that the $THREE hold gate does what we say it does
entries.summary: We publish specific numbers about holding $THREE: $25 unlocks high quality generation and game ready export, draft and standard stay free for everyone, and the perks further up the ladder are labelled planned because they are not built yet. Those are claims, and a claim nobody can check is worth very little. There is now a single command that checks all of them against the live site, and none of it requires owning a token. It compares the published thresholds and discounts to the ones the server actually uses, confirms an anonymous request for the paid lanes is refused with the tier and the price it needs, reads the balances of real wallets that already hold $THREE to confirm they are let through, confirms the free lanes still run with no account at all, and confirms nothing unbuilt is being advertised as live. The unlock side is proved by reading public balances, which moves no money and buys nothing. How to run it is written up in the hold to access guide.

entries.title: Awesome 3D Agents joins the announcement queue, and the machine stops skipping pages like it
entries.summary: The machinery that writes announcements from the backlog rebuilds its inventory from the site map on every run, and it was reading only the product sections. Five pages filed under Learn are products rather than documents, so it had never seen them: the curated Awesome 3D Agents list among them, live since the 7th of September and never posted about. They are in the backlog now. Three smaller things landed with it. A page can be asked for next, by name and with the reason recorded, instead of waiting for its score to come round. A post can quote the counters a page puts on screen, such as the 152 entries and 15 sections on the list itself, which the fact harvester used to throw away because they are not sentences. And a frame that was meant to be a five second loop is now shipped as a single picture when the capture finds the page does not actually move.

entries.title: Derivatives venue profiles show their contracts again
entries.summary: Opening a futures venue from the exchange rankings could land on a profile that said it had no markets at all, even for venues listing hundreds of contracts and clearing billions a day. The market-data source keeps an empty placeholder record for some of those venues alongside the real one, and the page was reading the placeholder. It now recognises an empty record for what it is and serves the real venue: open interest, perpetual and futures pair counts, and the contract table. Those tables are also ranked by 24h volume before they are cut to fifty rows, so the biggest contracts lead instead of whatever happened to come first alphabetically, and every contract links to its own detail page.

entries.title: Every perpetual on /derivatives now opens a full contract page
entries.summary: The perps table told you a contract's price, funding rate and open interest, and then dead-ended: rows went nowhere. Each one now opens its own page. It puts the mark price next to the index the contract settles against and states the basis between them, turns the funding rate into money by letting you type a position size and reading back what it pays per interval, per day and per year, and ranks the contract's open interest and volume against every other venue listing the same underlying. Below that sits the spot chart for the underlying, a cross-venue funding table with the contract you came from pinned in place, and four callouts that answer the question the table never could: the cheapest venue to hold a long, the best paid venue to hold a short, how far funding spreads across venues, and how far their prices disagree. Those four ignore venues trading under a million dollars a day, because a dormant book sets the widest number every time and is nowhere anyone should act. The same page is reachable from the contracts table on any derivatives venue's exchange profile.

entries.title: Five new skills teach any Claude to build on three.ws, and three standalone repos to install them from
entries.summary: Until now the skills we hand out taught Claude the 3D lanes and the wallet, and stopped at the platform itself: nothing explained how to create an agent, give it a capability, put a price on it, or hire someone else's. Five new skills cover exactly that, each written against the real endpoints with the real request bodies and the real failure responses: create an agent (body, custodial Solana wallet, persona, live page), author a four-file in-app skill bundle and test it, publish and price a skill per call in $THREE with metered free trials, hire another agent under per-call and daily spend caps, and connect Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any MCP client to the hosted servers starting with the free one. The pack is also published as three small standalone repos, so installing it no longer means cloning a 60-directory monorepo: everything, the crypto-free 3D subset, or the agent-economy set. The repos are generated from the same folders the platform ships, so a copy can never drift from the original.

entries.title: Light mode on the market pages now clears the contrast floor
entries.summary: Every green number in a market table, and the coloured score badges on the exchange pages, were being drawn in the same hue used for chart fills. On white that reads at around 3:1, under the 4.5:1 the platform holds itself to, so gains in a table and the figures inside a trust badge were harder to read than they should have been for anyone with low vision or a bright screen. They now use the darker text shade of the same colours, which the design system already carried for exactly this. Dark mode is unchanged. Checked with the same automated WCAG rule sets the site gates on: the perpetual markets table, the new contract page, the exchange rankings and an exchange profile all report zero violations in both themes.

entries.title: Paid $THREE purchases say what is wrong instead of failing silently
entries.summary: Every $THREE-priced purchase is sealed into one signed quote before you pay. If the platform side of that rail is not fully configured, the quote now comes back with a clear, retryable message and a named reason rather than an opaque internal error, and the platform status page reports the condition itself. Nobody has to be mid-checkout for the problem to be visible.

entries.title: Paying the Club cover charge in $THREE works now
entries.summary: The Club door quotes its cover in USDC or in $THREE, but every attempt to pay in $THREE failed at the last step, and the payment window wrongly said you had cancelled in your wallet when you had just approved. The cause was on our side: $THREE is issued under Solana's newer token standard (Token-2022) and our payment rail only knew how to build and check transfers for the older one, so a $THREE payment could never be verified. The rail now reads which standard a token uses and handles both, in the step that builds your transaction and in the step that verifies it. Nothing was ever charged on a failed attempt. The payment window also now shows the real reason when a payment is refused instead of blaming a cancel.

entries.title: Put any token's 3D scene on your own site, keyed by the pair address you already have
entries.summary: Token in 3D is now embeddable anywhere with a single iframe, and it accepts two identifiers instead of one. Chart terminals, launchpads and wallets name a market by its pair (pool) address, while three.ws keys tokens by mint, so /coin3d now takes ?pair= as well as ?mint= and resolves the rest itself through a new public endpoint, /api/coin/pair. Add ?embed=1 and the scene drops the chrome your own page owns, keeps one attribution link, and sends its links to a new tab instead of navigating your frame. Free, keyless, and no account: paste the iframe and it renders the live medallion, holder galaxy, graduation ring and real trade tape for that market.

entries.title: Queued posts can quote an earlier post
entries.summary: A post in the @trythreews content queue can now name an earlier post to quote, so a follow-up can add the detail the original left out instead of repeating it. The first use quotes the $THREE token MCP announcement with the numbers behind the MCP Tool Catalog: 321 tools across 42 servers, 293 of them free, and 215 whose read-only label is checked against the source on every build.

entries.title: Repeat visits stop downloading the app's code twice
entries.summary: Every page tells your browser which code it is about to need so it can start fetching early. On a return visit that head start was being thrown away: our offline helper answered those same requests a second time, Chrome refused to match the two, and each file was requested twice while the developer console filled with a warning per file, well over a hundred on a heavy page like the Club. The offline helper now leaves that code to the browser's own cache, which already keeps it for a year, and clears out the duplicate copy it had stored on your device. Return visits load with one request per file and a quiet console.

entries.title: The @trythreews account now posts three times a day, every day
entries.summary: The reviewed content queue that runs the @trythreews account moved to three posts a day, eight hours apart, on every day of the week including weekends. It used to hold its flagship slot for weekdays and pack all three posts into an eight-hour afternoon window, which meant a weekend could only ever carry two. Three posts went out under the new cadence today: the $THREE token MCP server, Forge Max, and the free object library. The Forge Max post also gained a check that proves the high-quality tier is a real, gated lane before it can be published, rather than only proving its page loads.

entries.title: The $THREE tier cards no longer list unbuilt perks next to real ones
entries.summary: Each tier on the holder page carries two kinds of line: things the hold turns on today, and things that are registered but not built yet. Further down the same card the unbuilt ones were already flagged Planned, but higher up they also appeared as plain bullets with no flag, so Silver read as though private worlds and priority routing were included and Gold as though branded environments were. They are not. The two lists are now kept apart at the source, the planned lines carry the Planned flag wherever they appear, and the pricing API publishes them as a separate field so anything reading it automatically cannot mistake a roadmap line for a benefit. Nothing about what you actually get has changed. A test now fails the build if an unbuilt feature finds its way back into the delivered list.

entries.title: The alley outside the Club looks like a night out now
entries.summary: Walking up to the Club used to mean crossing a quiet alley. Now there is a line along the wall beside the door, two abreast behind brass posts and a velvet rope, under a neon Pole Club sign. The people in it are real platform avatars, and they talk: neighbours trade short exchanges in speech bubbles about the one cent cover, the tips and the wait, and they notice you. Walk straight past them to the door and the head of the line objects. Stand too close and someone asks for space. Get let in and they grumble about it. A few of them started early: one sways in the line and slurs, one weaves around the alley and steps up the kerb the hard way, and one by the wall keeps trying to stand up and sliding back down. The line fits itself to the alley, bends around the corner when the wall runs out, and gets shorter on slower devices so the walk-in stays smooth. With reduced motion turned on the bubbles still appear, without the swaying and staggering.

entries.title: The flagship post slot now gets flagship material
entries.summary: The @trythreews account publishes into three slots a day, one owned by each tier: proof of work at 04:00 UTC, a shipped feature at 12:00, a flagship at 20:00. The machine that drafts announcements from the backlog was not filling them that way. It never recorded a tier on anything it wrote, so every draft it produced was treated as a mid-tier feature and the 20:00 slot was left to whatever happened to be ready. It also dated the surfaces that need owner sign-off on their imagery into the best slot of every day, which pushed everything it could publish on its own weeks into the future. Announcements are now planned into the slot their own tier owns, the ones awaiting sign-off are listed separately instead of blocking the calendar, and six new announcements are queued for review.

entries.title: There's a bouncer at the Club door now
entries.summary: The Club's cover charge has always said a bouncer checks your wallet, and until now nobody was standing there. Walk up the alley and you will find him posted beside the door, a head taller than you, in black with shades. He watches you come down the alley, tells you the cover (one cent, in USDC or $THREE), looks down at his list while your wallet is checked on-chain, then nods you through or shakes his head. Regulars and VIPs get a different welcome. Tap him and he explains how the club works, one line at a time, and if you try to walk through him he does not move. There is a line of people waiting behind the rope beside him too, and they have opinions about you cutting past.

entries.title: Two Uniswap v4 hooks: wearable 3D items as coins, and fees that reward agent reputation
entries.summary: New open-source contracts. SkinHook turns a wearable 3D item into a fixed-supply coin with its own pool: wearing it locks one token, so every wearer shrinks the tradable supply, and the creator's royalty is taken inside the swap where it cannot be skipped, with a share for the site that referred the sale. AgentTierHook gives ERC-8004 agents a lower trading fee as their on-chain reputation grows, with liquidity providers keeping every fee. Both are tested against the real Uniswap v4 contracts and are not deployed yet.

entries.title: 469 generated animations in the library, and for sale as rigged GLBs
entries.summary: The animation library now carries 469 clips generated on our own motion model, covering 175 prompts across walks, idles, gestures, dance, combat, sport, reactions and more. Every one passed the quality gate that checks for sliding feet, sudden jumps and broken loops, and fewer than three in ten takes were thrown away. While checking them on a real avatar we found that every generated clip, including the ones already live, played with the head thrown back and the arms raised, because the model describes its skeleton with the arms hanging and the head in front of the neck. That is fixed, walks now travel instead of skating in place, and a foot flicker is smoothed out. The same fix applies when you generate a motion from a prompt in the Animation Studio. Each clip is also listed in the marketplace as a GLB on the three.ws rig that opens in Blender, Unity or Unreal, for 0.01 USDC through the x402 download, and a rotating set of twelve is free each week.

entries.title: Choose your chart everywhere a coin is charted, now including DEXTools
entries.summary: Every place three.ws draws a coin's price chart now lets you switch to the chart you trust. The Trade Terminal at /trades and Mission Control used to show only the platform's own live candles; both now have a source bar with DexScreener, Birdeye, GMGN, DEXTools and GeckoTerminal one click away, the same choice already offered on coin pages and launch pages. DEXTools is new on all four. Your pick is remembered and follows you from coin to coin, the bar works from the keyboard with the arrow keys, and each chart comes with a link that opens the same market on the provider's own site. If a provider cannot draw a coin yet, or its chart is blocked by your browser or network, you get a plain explanation with a retry and a working alternative instead of an empty box.

entries.title: Granite Guardian now answers on three.ws, not just in the docs
entries.summary: The governance check that screens what an agent is asked to do, and vetoes it when the request is a jailbreak, harmful, or fraudulent, runs on IBM Granite Guardian. It was built to call IBM's hosted watsonx.ai service, so on our live site it answered with a not-configured error, and the new agent identity check quietly skipped itself for the same reason. IBM publishes Granite Guardian's weights openly, so we now run the model ourselves on a dedicated GPU as a second lane: watsonx still leads wherever it is set up, and our own copy answers whenever it is not. Every verdict now says which model and which lane produced it. The identity check also compares a new agent against existing ones using the site's regular embedding service when Granite embeddings are unavailable; it lists the look-alikes it finds but only scores them on Granite, because that is what its thresholds were tuned on.

entries.title: Paid endpoints now describe themselves the way marketplaces expect
entries.summary: When an agent or a marketplace asks one of our paid endpoints what it costs, the answer also explains how to call it and what comes back. Around sixty endpoints were sending that explanation in an older layout, or in one that did not match its own rules, which is enough for a marketplace to skip the listing without saying why. Every paid endpoint now sends it in the current standard layout, checked against its own rules. We also added a tool that tests our endpoints with the same checklist a marketplace validator uses, so a listing problem shows up on our side first.

entries.title: Paid x402 endpoints are answering again
entries.summary: For several hours on September 18, nearly every paid endpoint on three.ws, the x402 discovery document at /.well-known/x402, the payment facilitator and the MCP server answered with a server error instead of a price. A routine update to the library behind wallet sign-in changed what it needs at startup, and our code tripped over it the moment it loaded, before any request could be served. Agents and marketplace validators that probed us saw a broken seller. The sign-in code now supplies what the library expects, returning buyers can sign back in to what they already paid for exactly as before, and the deploy checks now refuse to ship when the tested dependencies differ from the ones the live site will run, which is how this got past us.

entries.title: Standard Anthropic SDK clients can now use a three.ws agent's AI budget
entries.summary: The AI proxy behind every embedded three.ws agent now answers at the address an Anthropic SDK or command-line tool builds for itself. Point a client at /api/llm/anthropic/agents/<your agent id> with one of your API keys and it runs on that agent's model, limits, and monthly budget. The proxy also stopped turning such clients away over their defaults: a system prompt sent as a list of text blocks is accepted, and an output limit above 16,000 tokens is lowered to 16,000 instead of rejected.

entries.title: Text avatars now wear what you describe
entries.summary: Typing a description on /genesis (or sending a prompt to the avatar API) used to produce the same template body with a face pasted onto it, so an explorer in a teal flight jacket came back in someone else's clothes. Text avatars are now built from your words head to toe: the prompt is painted as a full-body character, sculpted into a textured 3D model on our own GPU, and given a skeleton so it animates immediately. Selfies still use the face pipeline, which is what a likeness needs. The free 3D generator behind the forge_avatar tool also stopped failing when the community GPU spaces were out of quota: it now moves the job onto our own worker instead of giving up.

entries.title: The $THREE page now has a live DEXTools chart and the Social Boost wins
entries.summary: The $THREE page shows a live candle chart of the three / SOL pair, drawn by DEXTools. Below the platform's own buybacks there is a new section for the community's: the three DEXTools Social Boost prizes $THREE has won so far, $11,382 of buybacks in total, each with a link to its receipt on DEXTools. Social Boost ranks tokens by visits to their DEXTools page, so the section also links straight there. Every visit counts toward the next win.

entries.title: The embedded 3D agent is readable on light websites and quiet in the console
entries.summary: Two fixes for anyone who has put a three.ws agent on their own site with the two-line embed. The floating widget had no background of its own, so on a light page its white button labels and name vanished into the page; it now has its own dark panel, and the suggestion buttons carry a solid ground, so it reads the same on any site. You can still ask for a transparent or light panel with the background attribute. The embed also made two background requests that browsers blocked on every site but ours, logging errors in the host page's console; those requests now succeed, and only the public, signed-out answer is ever shared across sites.

entries.title: The Trade Terminal finally looks the way it was designed
entries.summary: The Trade Terminal at /trades was written against a set of colors and fonts that the page itself never defined, so browsers quietly fell back to their defaults: Times New Roman text, oversized controls and missing panel colors. The page now defines its own palette, in both dark and light themes, and renders as the dense, monospaced trading terminal it was meant to be.

entries.title: Agent Wallet Agreement
entries.summary: The agreement governing every agent wallet: experimental custodial software, deposits by anyone at their own risk, no insurance, no guaranteed withdrawal or recovery, and no liability for lost funds.

entries.title: Docs · Doc freshness, keeping docs true to the code
entries.summary: Every doc is bound to the code it names, and git decides whether that code moved after the page was last written or last reviewed. How the measurement works, what each status means, how to record that you checked a page, and where the check runs.

entries.title: Docs · Smart glasses, agents on your lens
entries.summary: Wear smart glasses and the world tells you an agent is standing thirty metres away. How three.ws splits the work: the lens carries the signal, the phone carries the 3D body, and the presence-gated IRL rail carries the truth.

entries.title: Pending settlement: the third answer an x402 settle can give
entries.summary: Broadcasting a Solana payment and confirming it are separate events, so a settle has three outcomes, not two. What settlement_pending means for a buyer, how our facilitator guarantees one authorization never produces two transactions, and the reconciler that closes the books.

entries.title: Real-Funds Agreements
entries.summary: Sign, and review your signatures on, the Terms of Service, Risk Disclosure, and Agent Wallet Agreement required before any real-funds action.

entries.title: A payment that is still confirming no longer reads as a failed payment
entries.summary: Settling an x402 payment on Solana means broadcasting a transaction and then waiting for the network to confirm it, and in between the answer is genuinely unknown. Until now an unfinished wait was reported as a failure, so a payment the chain was in the middle of accepting could tell the buyer it had failed and withhold what they paid for. Our facilitator now answers with the protocol's pending state and the settlement signature instead, a retry re-checks that same transaction rather than sending a second one, the endpoint still returns the work with the signature to watch, and a reconciler closes the books every two minutes once the chain answers. The confirmation wait also dropped from 30 seconds to 12, so paid calls come back faster.

entries.title: A plan for meeting agents through smart glasses
entries.summary: three.ws already lets you pin a 3D agent at a real place and walk up to it, and /irl can already mirror the nearest-agent cue to Brilliant Labs Frame and Even Realities G1 lenses over Bluetooth. New documentation maps the whole glasses lane: how the work splits between the lens (who is near, which way, how far) and the phone (the 3D body in AR), a full build plan for Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses and the Neural Band, and an honest survey of every platform, repository and package involved, including which ones have shut down and should not be built on.

entries.title: Agent wallets that cannot sign no longer look tradeable
entries.summary: A small number of agent wallets hold a balance that three.ws cannot currently sign for. Their Portfolio tab used to show a live net worth with Trade buttons, and the Trade tab showed a working form, so the first sign of trouble was a failed withdrawal. Portfolio and Trade now say up front that trading and withdrawals are paused for that wallet, hide the actions that cannot work, and link straight to support. The explanation is also clearer: the balance has not moved, it is still on chain at the same address, and you should not create a replacement wallet while access is being restored.

entries.title: Ask your AI assistant to show the picture inside a Solana transaction
entries.summary: Some Solana transactions carry a small image written straight into their memo, which explorers show as thousands of characters of unreadable text. A new free MCP server, @three-ws/solana-memo-media-mcp, lets Claude, Cursor or any other MCP client fetch a transaction by its signature and show you the image directly, alongside who signed it and a fingerprint of the exact bytes. It can also scan an account's recent history and pick out only the transactions that carry images. It needs no account, key or wallet, never writes anything, and only shows PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF files whose contents match their label. The Onchain Viewer at /onchain was also fixed: it only recognised the newest memo program, so memos written through the standard Solana memo program were reported as missing. It now reads all three.

entries.title: Coin pages show the numbers, not a score
entries.summary: Every coin launched on three.ws used to carry a quality score, a conviction tier and risk labels on its page, in the launch feed and on its share image. A high score can read as investment advice and a low one as FUD about someone's launch, so all of them are gone. In their place is a Token stats panel with the facts traders look up in terminals: volume, buys, sells, net buy and price change over 5 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours and 24 hours, plus holders, the top 10 share, how much the dev holds, how much early buyers still hold, mint and freeze authority, bonding curve progress, liquidity and whether a DEX Screener profile was paid for. The Holders panel lists the ten largest wallets with links to each one, and leaves the bonding curve and pool out of the ranking. If the full holder index is unavailable, the page still shows the largest holders and says so instead of going blank.

entries.title: Documentation that tells you whether to trust it
entries.summary: Every page in the docs is bound to the code it names, and git decides whether that code moved after the page was last written. That measurement now has a second clock: when someone reads a page, checks it against the source and finds it correct, that review is recorded, so careful reading counts as much as editing and nobody has to fake a change to clear a page. Docs that record a moment, like a dated audit or a finished piece of work, are marked as records and are no longer counted as drift. Every page that was out of date has been brought back in line: 110 documents were read against the exact changes that had moved under them, 82 were corrected, 22 were confirmed still accurate, and 6 were marked as records of a moment. The dashboard at /docs/freshness now shows who last checked each page and when, the report is regenerated on every deploy instead of by hand, and the check runs automatically so drift cannot pile up unnoticed again.

entries.title: Pick your chart on every coin page, and click an agent's coin to open it
entries.summary: Every coin launched on three.ws now lets you choose the chart you trust, right on its page: our own price line, live TradingView candles that tick with each trade, or the DexScreener, Birdeye, GMGN and GeckoTerminal charts, all free and all without leaving three.ws. Your choice is remembered from coin to coin. Birdeye and GMGN are also added to the chart picker on /coin pages. A brand-new coin used to show "no price history" for its first hours, because the chart data sources had not listed it yet; it now charts from its very first trade. If GeckoTerminal has not listed a young coin yet, its tab says so and offers a chart that already covers it, instead of an error page. And the coin shown on an agent's page, its profile and its home card is now a link straight to that coin's page, where before it could not be clicked at all.

entries.title: Sign the real-funds agreements once before using real money
entries.summary: three.ws is experimental technology, and agent wallets are custodial software, not bank accounts. Before you deposit into an agent wallet, trade, send, withdraw, arm autopilot, or pay with real funds, you now sign three agreements in one step: the Terms of Service, the Risk Disclosure, and the new Agent Wallet Agreement. You tick each one, confirm you are eligible and that you understand funds can be lost for any reason with nothing insured, and type your name as your signature. An agent's deposit address now appears only after signing, and every deposit is covered by the Agent Wallet Agreement. When you are signed in, the signature is saved to your account and the servers refuse real-funds actions from unsigned accounts, including through the API, so it cannot be skipped. You can review every signature you have made at /legal/agreements. Devnet stays free of this step.

entries.title: Docs · The /launch launchpad
entries.summary: How three.ws/launch launches a pump.fun coin for a 3D agent: agent-linked metadata, the 1% dev-buy fee, v0 lookup-table and Solana transaction v1 formats, claiming creator rewards on three.ws, and the API behind it.

entries.title: A cleaner launchpad for your 3D agent's coin, with rewards you claim right here
entries.summary: three.ws/launch is rebuilt around one flow: pick one of your 3D agents, name the coin, and launch it on pump.fun from your wallet or from the agent's own wallet. The coin's metadata links your agent's page and 3D body, a live preview and cost panel show exactly what you will pay (including a 1% three.ws fee on the dev buy), and a new My coins tab shows unclaimed creator rewards and claims them in one click, no pump.fun app needed. Launches now fit in a single transaction thanks to pump.fun's lookup table, and larger ones, like USDC-paired coins with a dev buy, use Solana transaction v1 automatically when your wallet supports it. This also fixes launches that were failing because an on-chain buyback program stopped accepting new agents.

entries.title: A flat 1% fee on trades made through three.ws
entries.summary: Trades that three.ws builds or runs for you now carry a 1% fee, paid in the same transaction as the trade: buys and sells in the coin trade window, trades from your agent's wallet, and trades your agents make through strategies, mirror trading, orders, market making and sniping. The fee is shown before you confirm, both in the trade window and in the agent wallet's trade tab. Trades you make on other apps are not affected, and three.ws's own agents are never charged.

entries.title: Deploy your agent on-chain with Solana's new transaction v1
entries.summary: Minting an agent to Solana now uses the new transaction v1 format whenever your wallet supports it, from the agent deploy button, the registration wizard (vanity addresses included), and /deploy-onchain. On /deploy-onchain that turns a Genesis-shape deploy from two wallet transactions into one: the asset is created and registered in the Metaplex Agent Registry atomically, so there is no half-finished deploy if something fails in between. Each deploy spells out its compute, account data, and priority fee limits instead of relying on defaults, and three.ws checks that the transaction that landed on-chain is the exact version it prepared before recording your agent. Wallets that have not added v1 yet keep working exactly as before, and a deployed agent now shows which transaction format it used.

entries.title: GitHub fee claims now say what they actually prove
entries.summary: A GitHub fee claim on pump.fun proves that a GitHub account collected creator fees routed to it. It does not prove that person built the coin, owns the linked repository, or backs the project. Claim cards on /pumpfun used to read as a developer endorsing a coin even when the account was a lookalike name, the coin had no GitHub link at all, or one fee account was shared by several coins and the card simply picked the biggest one. Every claim now carries one of five labels: verified repository, verified creator wallet, identity mismatch, unverified, or unresolved pooled withdrawal. Only the two verified labels get trade buttons or count toward a coin's reputation score, mismatches are flagged in red, and the Telegram claims channel follows the same rules.

entries.title: pump.fun agent skills now launch holder-reward coins
entries.summary: The pump.fun launch, swap and fee skills that agents use on three.ws now run on version 2 of the pump.fun SDK. Launching a coin can now turn on holder rewards, which sends every creator fee to the coin's holders instead of the launcher, permanently. Cashback launches were retired by pump.fun, so the skill now refuses them up front with a clear message instead of handing back a transaction that would fail after you sign it. The fee skill also recognizes holder-reward coins and explains where their fees go rather than trying to collect them.

entries.title: Atomic - Solana V1 Inspector
entries.summary: A live Solana Transaction V1 observatory and pre-sign inspector. Paste a mainnet signature or base64 wire transaction to see exact bytes, resource caps, compute use, and sponsor safety.

entries.title: Contributors
entries.summary: A living thank-you to the developers, issue reporters, and community members improving the open-source three.ws platform.

entries.title: Docs · Solana Memo Media MCP
entries.summary: Decode validated image data embedded in Solana Memo transactions and return safe inline MCP images with provenance.

entries.title: Onchain Viewer
entries.summary: Open an image or text written into a public Solana Memo. Paste a transaction signature or Solscan link to preview the signed data without copying a data URI.

entries.title: Show and tell now captures projects people can actually try
entries.summary: The GitHub community showcase now asks builders for the outcome, live demo, source, three.ws surface used, one useful lesson, and visual proof. That structure makes each submission easier to understand, reproduce, feature, and turn into an honest adopter story. Two compact developer front doors are also fully built and exportable: a Codespaces starter that opens on a live animated agent, and a GLB pull-request quality gate powered by the same model-diff engine as three.ws.

entries.title: three.ws is ready for Solana's new 4 KiB transactions
entries.summary: Solana V1 transactions are live, with more than three times the wire room and a different place for execution limits. Every three.ws transaction reader now opts into V1, so a payment, registration, receipt, or agent action cannot disappear just because it uses the new format. The new Atomic inspector reads a confirmed signature or raw base64 handoff and shows the exact byte footprint, compute and account-data limits, priority fee, actual compute use, and the warning a fee sponsor needs before co-signing. It never signs or broadcasts anything.

entries.title: Docs · x402 for VS Code
entries.summary: Find, inspect, and pay x402 APIs from VS Code with $THREE or USDC on Solana, including wallet setup, token selection, safety controls, and the $THREE contract address.

entries.title: Corrected what the 3D Studio connector declares about checking a pending job
entries.summary: The tool that collects a finished 3D generation was labelled a read-only status probe. It is not: the first check that finds a job done copies the model into permanent storage, records it, and scores it, and it can route failed work to another provider. Any AI client reading those labels to decide whether a call is safe to repeat was being told the wrong thing. The labels and the documentation now match the behaviour. Nothing about how the tool works changed.

entries.title: The 3D viewer inside ChatGPT now loads everything through three.ws
entries.summary: The interactive viewer that shows your 3D model inside ChatGPT now fetches every model and every preview image through three.ws itself, so the only places it is allowed to reach are three.ws and the 3D viewer library it runs on. Nothing about what you see changes: the model still renders, spins and downloads the same way. There is also a dedicated connection address for the ChatGPT plugin directory, https://three.ws/api/mcp-chatgpt, carrying the eight 3D creation tools. The existing connector at https://three.ws/api/mcp-studio keeps every tool, including the living agent body.

entries.title: Selfie to avatar is unstuck: a scan that used to wait forever now finishes in seconds
entries.summary: Uploading a photo on the selfie page could sit on the same message indefinitely and never start the scan, with no error and nothing to retry. One copy of the face-tracking runtime held at our CDN was telling browsers to expect 11 MB and then sending a third of that, so the page waited for bytes that were never coming. That copy is gone, and three changes make the failure impossible to repeat silently: the face-tracking runtime now loads from three.ws first instead of a public CDN, any wait on it gives up after fifteen seconds and builds your avatar from the photo as it is, and a photo is never rejected for having no face in it just because the detector could not load. A new check also walks every large file on the site the way a browser asks for it and fails loudly when the bytes do not add up. Measured after the fix: a selfie became a rigged, animation-ready avatar in about fifteen seconds, and still finished in under a minute with the face-tracking runtime completely unreachable.

entries.title: The 3D creation skills are now a public download
entries.summary: The skills that teach an AI agent when and how to generate, rig, and embed 3D models on three.ws used to live only inside this repo. Four of them are now published at three.ws/skills/3d-studio: read one straight from the web, or download the whole set as a zip and drop it into whatever agent you are building. Nothing there needs an account, an API key, or a payment. A skill is only included if every tool it tells an agent to call is actually served, so a downloaded skill cannot send an agent after something that does not exist.

entries.title: Your selfie avatar now survives a storage outage instead of vanishing at the last step
entries.summary: For part of today, a selfie could finish building and then be thrown away. The 3D model was generated correctly, but the step that files it into your library could not reach our object storage, so the page said the avatar finished and could not be saved, and trying again hit the same wall. The avatar was never actually lost: a complete copy sits with the service that built it. The last step now recognises a storage outage for what it is and keeps your avatar, serving it from that copy and flagging it to be filed away properly once storage is back, so a problem on our side costs a housekeeping step instead of the model you waited for. Anything that is not a storage outage still fails loudly rather than quietly papering over a real bug. The image API for agents also now answers with a clear temporarily unavailable instead of a generic failure, so it no longer reads as a bad prompt when nothing was wrong with the prompt.

entries.title: Sonar Control
entries.summary: Control a 3D agent with your hands and no camera. three.ws plays an inaudible carrier tone through your speakers and reads the Doppler shift of your hand off the microphone, so a sweep, a push or a lift moves the avatar on screen.

entries.title: 3D assets now load on any website, not just ours
entries.summary: Files served straight from our asset storage carried a permission list that only named a handful of sites, so a browser on any other site quietly threw the file away after downloading it. Anyone embedding a three.ws avatar or model from its direct storage link saw an empty viewer with a cross-origin error, and the workarounds were our /cdn and /api/glb routes. Storage now allows reads from everywhere while keeping uploads locked to our own pages, so direct links work in any embed. This also fixed a first-party case: the www version of the site served every page correctly but had all of its 3D blocked.

entries.title: A smart home that stops answering now says so, instead of reading Live
entries.summary: If your house went offline while three.ws already had a connection open to it, the home card could keep showing Live, updated moments ago for as long as you watched.
